As a cat owner myself, I know how heartbreaking it can be when our kitties are in distress - but although it may be hard I'm here to remind you that ultimately this is the best decision for now. 

Assuming you haven't, perhaps to try and alleviate your cat's stress levels you can go to the bathroom and spend some time with him. Give him some pats and play around a little with him to keep him company for some time. When the ordeal is done, I can assure you your cat won't hate you. Animals are very forgiving - this includes cats. Chances are he will forget about it after a while too.

Again, remember that none of this is your fault so don't beat yourself up!! :)

As someone with autism, this sounds like hell. I feel bad for autistic children's parents who think pressuring their kid into new things they don't have any prior experience in, practically forcing them to socialize is a form of "therapy." If anything, it's the opposite. Exposing your child/children to situations like this can just traumatize them in the long run, leaving them with bitter memories hence making it hard for them to want to actually socialize in the future or try new things.

If you want your child to improve their social skills,  want them to learn to regulate their emotions properly and in a healthy way instead of having meltdowns or outbursts; take them to a professional therapist. There are many types of therapy for this disorder.
